verdict.rationale: Reflect's site describes an open-source app that stores notes as local Markdown files and offers sync through iCloud Drive or Git rather than a vendor backend, which points to running without Reflect's cloud. But these are brief marketing lines, and other first-party docs describe a vendor-server architecture: an API at reflect.app/api, server-side end-to-end-encrypted note storage, and audio uploaded for background transcription. That leaves the extent of a true no-vendor-cloud mode unclear. Missing for 10: documented local-only setup and its feature limits, explicit self-hosted sync backend instructions (e.g. pointing Git sync at a user-operated remote), clarity on which features still require vendor servers, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can run the whole system without the vendor's cloud — local-only mode or a self-hosted sync backend I operate myself

citations.quote: An open-source note-taking app with daily notes, backlinks, and local Markdown files.
